Use these benchmark-specific domain hints only when the trigger matches:
- hover.title_terms_are_evidence (title/alias retrieval): Trigger: Claim or summary has proper nouns, aliases, parentheticals, work titles, dates. Hint: Treat Wikipedia article titles as evidence. Preserve canonical title words, aliases, disambiguators, proper nouns, and years in summaries and retrieval queries. Risk: Title matching can swamp the missing relation.
- hover.target_unresolved_claim_part (multi-hop residual): Trigger: Hop-1 or hop-2 already covers part of the claim. Hint: Split the claim into resolved and unresolved parts. The next query should target the missing supporting title, not restate the whole claim or only repeat already grounded entities. Risk: Bad earlier summary causes drift.
- hover.keep_relation_anchor (relation anchors): Trigger: Claim edge includes directed, founded, located in, brother, spouse, released, won, member of, occupation. Hint: Keep one relation anchor that connects the unresolved hop. Combine it with the discriminative entity/title/date rather than a long natural-language claim. Risk: Too many relation words make broad BM25 queries.
- hover.corrected_title_from_summary (summary corrections): Trigger: Intermediate summary corrects or clarifies a title/name/date from the claim. Hint: If a summary corrects a title, spelling, alias, or date, use the corrected surface in the next query while preserving enough claim context to verify/refute. Risk: May follow an incorrect summary correction.
- hover.corpus_time_floor (corpus time): Trigger: Claim mentions current, recent, or post-2017 facts under fixed Wikipedia abstracts. Hint: Remember the retrieval corpus may be time-bounded. Keep years as standalone query tokens and avoid treating missing post-corpus evidence as definitive. Risk: Only valid for fixed 2017-style corpora.
- hover.title_prefixed_summary (evidence provenance): Trigger: Summarization module over titled passages. Hint: Prefix key evidence with the passage title or entity label. Mark no-overlap passages as irrelevant instead of blending them into the summary. Risk: Extra title text can pollute later query if not concise.
Use these hints to choose compact, title-like query terms for missing supporting evidence. Apply these as conditional rules only: if a hint conflicts with explicit claim/source evidence, follow the explicit evidence, and do not change the required output format.
